question: The Greek Ministry of Education’s recent circular on special needs support in mainstream schools raises serious concerns about the effective implementation of inclusive education, as it may undermine the quality and consistency of the support provided to pupils with recognised special educational needs.

Similar challenges have been reported in other Member States, such as Ireland and Romania, where insufficient staff numbers and training make it difficult to ensure that all pupils have equal access to education.

The Council Recommendation on Pathways to School Success (2022) and Regulation (EU) 2021/817 on Erasmus+ underline the importance of mainstreaming and quality education, in the context of creating a fully functioning European Education Area. At the same time, the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights enshrines the right of every person to education without discrimination. Can the Commission say: 1.

How does it intend to strengthen the implementation of inclusive education in the Member States, addressing issues such as the lack of qualified staff and the qualitative assessment of special needs support in mainstream schools?
Does it plan to develop a common European framework for monitoring progress, in line with the Council Recommendation on Pathways to School Success?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.12.2025) In full respect of the division of competences in education set out in Article 165 of Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union1, the Commission promotes inclusive education under European Education Area (EEA) through initiatives such as Pathways to School Success2, aimed at improving learning outcomes for all learners.

Recommended measures include support to learners with disabilities or special educational needs in mainstream schools through accessible environments and learning materials, diverse teaching methods, and teacher training.
The Commission supports implementation by fostering mutual learning within EEA Working Groups3, providing policy guidance4 to Member States, and promoting progress towards EEA targets and indicators.

The Commission continues to implement the EU Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2021-20305, also guided by the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD)6, to which the EU and Member States are parties to the extent of respective competencies.

The Strategy promotes inclusive and accessible education and calls on Member States to ensure their education systems at all levels comply with the UNCRPD to advance on supported learning in inclusive mainstream settings7. Furthermore, EU Cohesion Policy Funds can support accessible infrastructure and teaching methods and technologies tailored to diverse learners.

Inclusion is also one of the priorities of Erasmus+ programme, which supports cooperation among stakeholders for developing innovative teaching materials enhancing inclusion, and for building capacities, while seeking to promote equal opportunities and access to organisations and participants with fewer opportunities themselves.
